content.comment_body: This [product_name] software version changes the color of some connection lines from black to red or blue after running a simulation. Some connections keep these simulation colors when returning to editing mode. The main issue is that printed schematics show these colored lines instead of black. To fix this, I've had to delete and redraw the connections, which is very time-consuming and it's easy to overlook a connection. Has anyone encountered this problem and found a solution?

Hello [user_name], I've encountered a similar issue as you described in my work with [product_name] as well. For internal documentation, I mostly use printed sheets myself, along with an electric scheme and an explanation of the electrical installation's functionality. Schematics printed with [product_name] software are considered intellectual property at my company, though sometimes these prints are included in client documentation.

Hello everyone! This is an important topic. It was discussed on the German forum under the link [url]. This color change error in [product_name] version [version_no] happens if: - You close the software while simulation is running - The software or Windows crashes during simulation - You save the program while simulation is running - You simulate more than one program at once and any of the above happens The issue is that the software saves the line color settings with the program itself. The steps below are a bit lengthy but solve the issue. I've translated them here—feel free to print them out for reference! 1) Open your affected program 2) Zoom out until you see the entire program 3) Go to TOOL --> OPTIONS --> COLOURS, select BLACK for simulation colors and APPLY/OK 4) Make a small change in the program (add and delete a block or move one slightly) 5) Start SIMULATION mode and check all lines are black 6) While simulation is running, close the software 7) When asked to save because of changes, select YES and save (either same or new file) 8) Reopen the software—make sure it's the only open instance! 9) Open your newly saved program 10) Return to TOOLS --> OPTIONS --> COLOURS and set the standard colors for everything, then APPLY/OK 11) Repeat this for every affected program, since the error is saved in each one—not just a global setting Hope this helps! A key lesson: Always stop simulation and return to editing mode (ensuring lines turn black) before saving or making any changes. Also, only run one simulation at a time. This is good programming practice. Good luck managing the color changes!
Thank you for sharing an effective solution to my frustrating issue. That makes sense. Have a good day!

analysis.insight_summary: Users reported a recurring problem in [product_name] version [version_no], where connection lines change color after simulation. These undesired colors persist when returning to editing, causing schematics to print in non-standard colors. Prior workarounds involved manually deleting and redrawing lines, which was inefficient and error-prone. The main usability challenge is that temporary simulation visuals impact permanent documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want simulation modes to be visually temporary, with all schematics defaulting to standard black connections in editing and printing. They expect a simple workflow, without needing time-consuming manual corrections.
